10 Vitamins You Should Never Take These dangerous vitamins are not beneficial to your health!

On the contrary, they often have the opposite effect. They're used because they are often cheap and create a huge profit margin for the manufacturer.

- Synthetic vitamin A: can also interfere with vitamin D and K2, increasing the risk of bone fractures

- Beta-carotene: made from coal tar and petroleum, it can increase the risk of certain cancers

- Folic acid: 30% to 40% of the world's population has an alteration of the MTHFR gene, which interferes with their ability to turn folic acid into folate. This causes it to build up in the blood and leads to an increased risk of cancer and a suppressed immune system.

- Synthetic B12: consuming large amounts depletes you of methylcobalamin, a vital antioxidant

- Calcium carbonate: can build up in the arteries and kidneys and increase your risk of a heart attack

- Iron: too much can increase your risk of type 2 diabetes, liver issues, Parkinson's, and Alzheimer's

- Magnesium oxide: a cheap, poorly-absorbed form of magnesium that frequently causes diarrhea

- Vitamin D2: not nearly as beneficial as vitamin D3, yet it's the most prescribed form

- Omega-6 fat, often in the form of linoleic acid: too much can increase inflammation

- Copper: high amounts can be toxic

videos.title: 12.11.26 - RIFT Presentation
videos.summary_source_text:
12.11.26 - RIFT Presentation RIFT is a modern, non-custodial trading and financial technology ecosystem designed to bring together market access, education, intelligent execution, portfolio participation and professional trading infrastructure in one connected environment.

Built for both newcomers and experienced market participants, RIFT provides a structured journey from learning and practice through to increasingly sophisticated forms of market participation.

ONE ECOSYSTEM. MULTIPLE WAYS TO PARTICIPATE.

RIFT gives users access to a range of trading and financial tools, including:

• Demo Trading — Practice market participation using virtual capital while learning how markets, execution and platform functionality work.

• Spot Trading — Participate directly in spot markets while developing an understanding of market behaviour, patience and risk management.

• Futures Trading — Access leveraged markets with tools and functionality designed for more advanced trading strategies and risk management.

• Smart Money — Explore structured portfolio participation through features including mirror wallets and trading books, allowing users to move beyond focusing only on individual trades.

• Auto Trading Engine — Access structured automated execution through different environments designed to support systematic and repeatable participation.

• Prediction Markets — Participate in an emerging category of market infrastructure where users can trade contracts based on the probability of future events and outcomes.

• Prop Trading Infrastructure — Learn about and participate in the evolving world of proprietary trading, funded accounts, capital allocation, performance evaluation and professional risk management.

INTELLIGENT FINANCIAL INFRASTRUCTURE

RIFT is designed around the idea that the future of finance will combine human decision-making with intelligent technology.

Modern financial markets generate enormous amounts of information. Algorithms and AI systems can process data, identify patterns, monitor markets and support execution at a speed that is impossible for an individual human to replicate.

RIFT explores how these technologies can work alongside human judgement to create more structured and intelligent financial participation.

The objective is not simply to automate everything.

It is to combine people, data, technology, risk management and intelligent execution within a connected financial ecosystem.

EDUCATION AT THE CORE

RIFT places strong emphasis on education and developing a deeper understanding of financial markets.

Through the RIFT Before You Quit educational series, training sessions and community learning, participants explore subjects including:

• Trading psychology
• Risk management
• Capital preservation
• Portfolio construction
• Capital allocation
• Market structure
• Smart money concepts
• Futures and leverage
• Prediction markets
• Proprietary trading
• Behavioural finance
• Artificial intelligence
• Algorithmic execution
• Financial infrastructure
• Professional trading principles

The objective is to help participants understand not only how to participate in markets, but also why disciplined decision-making matters.

A STRUCTURED LEARNING JOURNEY

RIFT is designed to provide a progression from education and practice toward more advanced market participation:

Learn → Demo → Spot → Futures → Smart Money → Automated Execution → Professional Trading

Each stage introduces different concepts, technologies and levels of responsibility.

Rather than focusing solely on individual trades or short-term results, RIFT encourages participants to develop a broader understanding of risk, process, discipline and capital management.

NON-CUSTODIAL INFRASTRUCTURE

RIFT follows a non-custodial approach designed to give users greater control over their own funds and reduce the need to place assets into a centralized company-controlled account.

This reflects a broader movement within digital finance toward greater transparency, user control and blockchain-based infrastructure.

ACCESS FROM ANY DEVICE

RIFT is available through the web as well as its broader platform environment, making it accessible across modern computers, smartphones and other devices.

Its lightweight infrastructure is designed to make participation practical even for users with older devices, helping remove unnecessary technology barriers to accessing modern financial tools.

THE FUTURE OF FINANCIAL PARTICIPATION

Financial markets are changing rapidly.

Trading is becoming increasingly automated. Artificial intelligence is transforming data analysis. Prediction markets are creating new forms of information-based participation. Proprietary trading is expanding access to structured capital allocation models. Blockchain infrastructure is changing how digital assets can be held and transferred.

RIFT brings these developments together within one evolving ecosystem.

Philip NO-berg?! Ref Calls It a Goal but Crossbar Says No! #nhlshorts What a wild overtime sequence! Philip Broberg sends the puck toward the net and it hits the crossbar, but the referee immediately signals a goal, leaving everyone confused. After a video review, the officials overturn the call and rule that the puck never crossed the goal line. The potential overtime winner is taken off the board, but the St. Louis Blues still find a way to get the job done, coming out on top in the shootout!

videos.summary_source_text:
Avalanche Lose MacKinnon & Makar, Mount a 3rd Period Comeback Only to Lose in OT Colorado Avalanche fight for a point as Nathan MacKinnon and Cale Makar exit with concerning injuries. Can the Avs weather the storm without their superstar duo?

Chris Micieli and Zach Pearson break down the overtime loss to the Ottawa Senators, dissecting Parker Kelly’s high-risk turnover, special teams breakthroughs—including shorthanded and power play goals—and Scott Wedgewood’s turbulent night in net. The conversation explores the Avalanche’s ongoing struggles with slow starts, penalty trouble, and inconsistent in-game tempo, while also spotlighting critical moments like Nazem Kadri’s costly penalty and Ottawa’s aggressive late-game push. Listener reactions, potential lineup shakeups, and what’s next for Jared Bednar’s squad round out a must-listen episode for Avs fans bracing for the road ahead.

videos.title: Hindi 12.11.26 - RIFT Presentation
videos.summary_source_text:
Hindi 12.11.26 - RIFT Presentation RIFT is a modern, non-custodial trading and financial technology ecosystem designed to bring together market access, education, intelligent execution, portfolio participation and professional trading infrastructure in one connected environment.

Built for both newcomers and experienced market participants, RIFT provides a structured journey from learning and practice through to increasingly sophisticated forms of market participation.

ONE ECOSYSTEM. MULTIPLE WAYS TO PARTICIPATE.

RIFT gives users access to a range of trading and financial tools, including:

• Demo Trading — Practice market participation using virtual capital while learning how markets, execution and platform functionality work.

• Spot Trading — Participate directly in spot markets while developing an understanding of market behaviour, patience and risk management.

• Futures Trading — Access leveraged markets with tools and functionality designed for more advanced trading strategies and risk management.

• Smart Money — Explore structured portfolio participation through features including mirror wallets and trading books, allowing users to move beyond focusing only on individual trades.

• Auto Trading Engine — Access structured automated execution through different environments designed to support systematic and repeatable participation.

• Prediction Markets — Participate in an emerging category of market infrastructure where users can trade contracts based on the probability of future events and outcomes.

• Prop Trading Infrastructure — Learn about and participate in the evolving world of proprietary trading, funded accounts, capital allocation, performance evaluation and professional risk management.

INTELLIGENT FINANCIAL INFRASTRUCTURE

RIFT is designed around the idea that the future of finance will combine human decision-making with intelligent technology.

Modern financial markets generate enormous amounts of information. Algorithms and AI systems can process data, identify patterns, monitor markets and support execution at a speed that is impossible for an individual human to replicate.

RIFT explores how these technologies can work alongside human judgement to create more structured and intelligent financial participation.

The objective is not simply to automate everything.

It is to combine people, data, technology, risk management and intelligent execution within a connected financial ecosystem.

EDUCATION AT THE CORE

RIFT places strong emphasis on education and developing a deeper understanding of financial markets.

Through the RIFT Before You Quit educational series, training sessions and community learning, participants explore subjects including:

• Trading psychology
• Risk management
• Capital preservation
• Portfolio construction
• Capital allocation
• Market structure
• Smart money concepts
• Futures and leverage
• Prediction markets
• Proprietary trading
• Behavioural finance
• Artificial intelligence
• Algorithmic execution
• Financial infrastructure
• Professional trading principles

The objective is to help participants understand not only how to participate in markets, but also why disciplined decision-making matters.

A STRUCTURED LEARNING JOURNEY

RIFT is designed to provide a progression from education and practice toward more advanced market participation:

Learn → Demo → Spot → Futures → Smart Money → Automated Execution → Professional Trading

Each stage introduces different concepts, technologies and levels of responsibility.

Rather than focusing solely on individual trades or short-term results, RIFT encourages participants to develop a broader understanding of risk, process, discipline and capital management.

NON-CUSTODIAL INFRASTRUCTURE

RIFT follows a non-custodial approach designed to give users greater control over their own funds and reduce the need to place assets into a centralized company-controlled account.

This reflects a broader movement within digital finance toward greater transparency, user control and blockchain-based infrastructure.

ACCESS FROM ANY DEVICE

RIFT is available through the web as well as its broader platform environment, making it accessible across modern computers, smartphones and other devices.

Its lightweight infrastructure is designed to make participation practical even for users with older devices, helping remove unnecessary technology barriers to accessing modern financial tools.

THE FUTURE OF FINANCIAL PARTICIPATION

Financial markets are changing rapidly.

Trading is becoming increasingly automated. Artificial intelligence is transforming data analysis. Prediction markets are creating new forms of information-based participation. Proprietary trading is expanding access to structured capital allocation models. Blockchain infrastructure is changing how digital assets can be held and transferred.

RIFT brings these developments together within one evolving ecosystem.

Financial markets are changing rapidly.

Trading is becoming increasingly automated. Artificial intelligence is transforming data analysis. Prediction markets are creating new forms of information-based participation. Proprietary trading is expanding access to structured capital allocation models. Blockchain infrastructure is changing how digital assets can be held and transferred.

RIFT brings these developments together within one evolving ecosystem.

RIFT — THE NEXT-GEN AFFILIATE OS

Learn. Participate. Manage Risk. Think Bigger.

videos.title: Fix Your Slice With the 9 & 3 O’Clock Check
videos.summary_source_text:
Fix Your Slice With the 9 & 3 O’Clock Check If you’re fighting a slice, check your clubface at 9 o’clock and 3 o’clock.
At 9 o’clock, you don’t want the face hanging wide open. Then as you swing through to 3 o’clock, let the club rotate naturally while the path works slightly out to the right.

A lot of golfers try to fix a slice by just swinging farther right, but if the face is still open, the ball is still going right.

Get the face and path working together and you can start turning that slice into a draw.
The Blue Brick makes this easy to practice because it gives you something to swing around. Set it down, let the club work through its natural arc, and miss the brick on the way through.

19-year-old Blades Brown GOES LOW on Thursday | Austin Championship | 2026 Less than one week after getting his first PGA Tour win, Blades Brown shoots a 7-under 65 in the first round of the 2026 Austin Championship presented by Compliance Solutions. He is the youngest winner on PGA Tour since 1983.

The PGA Tour returns to Austin for the inaugural Austin Championship presented by Compliance Solutions, with the FedExCup Fall reaching its penultimate event at Omni Barton Creek. Fresh off a historic maiden victory in Mexico, teenage sensation Blades Brown headlines the field alongside Austin Smotherman, who arrives chasing a third consecutive win after triumphs in Utah and Bermuda. Ryan Gerard, Jackson Koivun and University of Texas alumni Pierceson Coody and Doug Ghim add further quality. With 2027 Tour status and places in next season’s Signature Events still up for grabs, the battle around the FedExCup top-100 and top-60 cut-offs are reaching a crucial stage.

videos.title: Legal… But Should It Be? The Vice Neon Sunset Problem
videos.summary_source_text:
Legal… But Should It Be? The Vice Neon Sunset Problem Does your golf ball's paint change where it goes? We tested the two-tone Vice Neon Sunset on the robot, and turning it around moved it about 8.5 yards.

📰 TaylorMade sues Callaway over "mud ball" paint claims: https://mygolfspy.com/news-opinion/taylormade-sues-callaway-over-chrome-tour-claims-alleging-false-advertising-and-a-mud-ball-campaign/
🧪 We tested the Polara anti-slice ball: https://mygolfspy.com/labs/polara-golf-ball-test-mygolfspy/

Tony Covey and Andrew Zanzig dig into the USGA's symmetry rule, written in 1981 to stop the Polara, and why a ball can pass as written but still not pass the spirit of the rule. Teed one way, the Neon Sunset faded. Flipped, 11 of 12 balls drew. It's still on the USGA's conforming list. Should it be?

videos.title: My #1 Homemade Broth for Collagen, Joints, and Skin | Dr. Mandell
videos.summary_source_text:
My #1 Homemade Broth for Collagen, Joints, and Skin | Dr. Mandell Many people pass up chicken feet without realizing they’re made largely of skin, tendons, ligaments, and cartilage—connective tissues that contain collagen. When slowly simmered, this tissue softens and releases gelatin into the broth, giving it a rich, satisfying texture. Collagen is a structural protein found in cartilage and other connective tissues, and it contains amino acids such as glycine and proline. Researchers have studied how collagen from food is digested and absorbed, and how gelatin or collagen supplements may relate to collagen production and joint comfort. In one human study, researchers detected collagen-derived peptides in the blood after volunteers consumed gelatin hydrolysates made from several sources, including chicken feet.  In this video, I take a closer look at this traditional food, how it’s used in broth, and why collagen-rich foods continue to interest people thinking about joint and connective-tissue health.

PubMed references:

Iwai K, et al. Identification of food-derived collagen peptides in human blood after oral ingestion of gelatin hydrolysates. J Agric Food Chem. 2005;53(16):6531–6536. PMID: 16076145. 

Shaw G, et al. Vitamin C-enriched gelatin supplementation before intermittent activity augments collagen synthesis. Am J Clin Nutr. 2017;105(1):136–143. PMID: 27852613.

Instagram:  https://www.instagram.com/motivationaldoc/ Many people pass up chicken feet without realizing they’re made largely of skin, tendons, ligaments, and cartilage—connective tissues that contain collagen. When slowly simmered, this tissue softens and releases gelatin into the broth, giving it a rich, satisfying texture. Collagen is a structural protein found in cartilage and other connective tissues, and it contains amino acids such as glycine and proline. Researchers have studied how collagen from food is digested and absorbed, and how gelatin or collagen supplements may relate to collagen production and joint comfort. In one human study, researchers detected collagen-derived peptides in the blood after volunteers consumed gelatin hydrolysates made from several sources, including chicken feet.  In this video, I take a closer look at this traditional food, how it’s used in broth, and why collagen-rich foods continue to interest people thinking about joint and connective-tissue health.

videos.summary_source_text:
Daiyan Henley trade CANCELLED, George Paton & the Denver Broncos come up empty at the trade deadline The Denver Broncos’ trade for Daiyan Henley is OFFICIALLY CANCELLED! What went wrong with the deal, and did Sean Payton and George Paton make the right decisions at the NFL trade deadline? With Denver pushing for a Super Bowl run, did the Broncos do enough to improve their roster, or did they miss a major opportunity?

The DNVR Broncos Podcast breaks down the cancelled Daiyan Henley trade, Denver’s overall trade deadline strategy, and what the front office’s decisions mean for the rest of the season. Should the Broncos have prioritized adding another defensive playmaker, or were there bigger needs elsewhere on the roster?

Plus, should the Denver Broncos have traded for a running back to help Bo Nix and the offense? We discuss why Denver decided against adding another RB, whether the Broncos have enough talent in their backfield, and how the decision could impact Sean Payton’s offense moving forward.

With the Broncos looking to establish themselves as legitimate AFC contenders, we debate whether Denver’s trade deadline approach was the right move for a team with Super Bowl aspirations. Did George Paton make the smart decision by standing pat, or will the Broncos regret not making another blockbuster trade?

videos.title: Best Home Ab Workout // Just 10 Min // 6 PACK GUARANTEED!
videos.summary_source_text:
Best Home Ab Workout // Just 10 Min // 6 PACK GUARANTEED! If you are looking for the best home ab workout you can do without any equipment, this 10 minute follow along routine is a great place to start. In this video, I’m going to take you through seven bodyweight ab exercises that you can do in the comfort of your own home, whether you are a beginner or an experienced lifter.

Get a flat stomach here - https://athleanx.com/flatstomach
Subscribe to this channel here - http://bit.ly/2b0coMW

The key to a successful home abs workout is keeping it simple enough to do consistently while making sure the exercises challenge your core. You don’t need an ab machine, a set of dumbbells or a gym membership. Every exercise in this routine uses your own bodyweight, and all you need is enough floor space to move comfortably.

The structure of the ab workout is simple.

There are 7 exercises, each performed for 60 seconds. If you are a beginner and cannot make it through the entire minute, perform the exercise for as long as you can with good form. Take a brief break when needed and rejoin the workout when you are ready. Your goal is to gradually build up the strength and endurance to complete more of each interval without sacrificing the quality of your reps.

Some of the exercises are divided into 30 seconds on each side or in each direction. These changes are noted below and demonstrated in the video so you can follow along without stopping to figure out what comes next.

Between exercises, you will get 30 seconds to rest. During that time, I’ll explain the next movement and show you how to perform it. This makes the routine easy to save and come back to whenever you want an ab workout at home that takes the guesswork out of your training.

Here is how the workout breaks down:

1. Ab Halos - 30 seconds clockwise / 30 seconds counterclockwise | 30 seconds rest
2. Frog Crunches - 60 seconds | 30 seconds rest
3. Russian Rows - 60 seconds | 30 seconds rest
4. Thread the Needle - 30 seconds each side | 30 seconds rest
5. Black Widow Knee Slides - 60 seconds | 30 seconds rest
6. Frog Circles - 60 seconds | 30 seconds rest
7. Sliding Ab Tucks - 60 seconds

Remember, the goal is not to rush through as many reps as possible just to keep moving for the full minute. Focus on controlling each rep and making your abs do the work. A shorter interval performed well gives you a better starting point than forcing yourself through an exercise after you have lost control of the movement.

What makes this home ab workout effective is the variety of ways you are challenging your core. Instead of repeating the same crunch over and over, you will work through movements that involve curling, rotation and maintaining control of your trunk as your arms and legs move. Pay attention to the demonstrations so you understand what each exercise should look like before your next interval begins.

One of the problems with many ab workouts is that people focus on moving their legs without paying attention to what their pelvis and lower back are doing. Your hip flexors naturally contribute to certain movements, but simply swinging your legs through a rep is not the same thing as deliberately training your abs.

Watch the position of your body, control the movement and follow the form cues throughout the video. If you can no longer maintain that control, pause and reset. Don’t assume that making an exercise faster or forcing a bigger range of motion will make it a better ab exercise.

People often ask how often they should train their abs. The first step is finding a routine you can perform consistently and recover from. Having a short, no equipment ab workout ready to go makes that easier. You can fit it around your regular workouts or do it at home when getting to the gym is not an option.

As you improve, use the same routine to measure your progress. Can you complete more of the interval with clean reps? Can you take fewer breaks without rushing? Can you maintain better control from the first exercise to the last? Those are useful signs that your core strength and endurance are improving.

Of course, building your abs and revealing your abs are two parts of the same goal. This workout can help you train your abdominal muscles, but getting visible six pack abs also depends on your overall body fat levels. Pair your training with a consistent approach to nutrition instead of expecting an ab workout alone to reveal your six pack.

videos.title: Why Sam Altman & Jony Ive Built Screenless AI Device
videos.summary_source_text:
Why Sam Altman & Jony Ive Built Screenless AI Device https://openart.ai/home?utm_source=youtube&utm_medium=influencer&utm_campaign=infl-youtube--na-acq-web&ref=BitBiasedAI-sd25

OpenAI is reportedly building a mysterious $200–$400 AI device with no screen, a voice-first interface, and potentially a camera, environmental sensors, and human-like memory. Sam Altman and legendary Apple designer Jony Ive are behind the project. But there's a major problem: almost everything you've seen about this device could be a rumor, an unverified leak, or an outright fake.

After OpenAI's roughly $6.5 billion acquisition of Jony Ive's AI hardware startup io in May 2025, speculation exploded about what could become OpenAI's first major consumer hardware product. Some reports describe a small, doughnut-shaped or hockey-puck-like AI companion. Others suggest a device that understands its surroundings, remembers conversations, and proactively helps you throughout the day.

But how much of that is actually real?

We break down the credible reporting from Bloomberg, The Verge, MacRumors, and other outlets to separate confirmed developments from anonymous leaks and viral misinformation.

According to reports, OpenAI's mysterious device could feature microphones, speakers, indicator lights, mechanical movement, and possibly a camera. It would likely rely heavily on cloud-based AI rather than running a powerful model entirely on the device. Reported pricing ranges from approximately $200 to $400, with the latest timeline pointing toward early 2027.

And that's where things get complicated.

A screenless ChatGPT device sounds compelling until you consider the limitations. How do you navigate maps, read documents, or review charts without a display? Can an always-listening assistant protect your privacy? What happens when cloud latency interrupts conversations? And can a small battery realistically support continuous AI-powered vision?

Then there's the biggest promise: proactive AI memory.

Reports suggest OpenAI wants an assistant that remembers important details, understands context, and offers help before you even ask. But delivering that experience requires reliable long-term memory, environmental awareness, accurate reasoning, and the ability to take actions without becoming intrusive.

Today's consumer AI devices haven't demonstrated that complete experience reliably.

We also examine Sam Altman's history of ambitious technology investments, from OpenAI and custom AI chips to Helion, Worldcoin, and brain-computer interfaces. His willingness to make enormous bets helps explain why OpenAI is entering the notoriously difficult hardware market.

Jony Ive brings another dimension. After helping shape Apple's iMac, iPod, iPhone, iPad, and Apple Watch, he's now involved in designing a new kind of AI product through LoveFrom. But can world-class industrial design overcome the technical and economic challenges that defeated earlier AI gadgets?

The Humane AI Pin launched at $699 plus a subscription. The Rabbit R1 promised an alternative to smartphone interactions. Both faced criticism over limited functionality and questionable everyday usefulness.

OpenAI will need to prove its device offers something meaningfully better.

We also investigate the viral fake OpenAI Super Bowl advertisement, the mysterious "Dime" puck renders, and the difference between official announcements and convincing fan-made concepts.

Beyond the hardware, there's a much bigger strategic question.

Apple and Google currently control the dominant mobile platforms through which millions of people access AI. An OpenAI-owned device could establish a direct relationship with consumers, potentially connect to ChatGPT subscriptions, and reduce dependence on those platforms.

But hardware manufacturing, cloud inference costs, battery limitations, and privacy concerns could make that strategy extremely expensive.

So is OpenAI preparing the next major shift in personal computing, or another ambitious AI gadget that struggles to justify its existence?

And would you actually pay $300 for a screenless AI companion when ChatGPT already works on your smartphone?

Share your thoughts in the comments, and subscribe to BitBiased for evidence-based coverage of OpenAI, artificial intelligence, emerging technology, and the biggest developments shaping the future of AI.

CHAPTERS

01:05 The Mysterious Device

04:38 The Features, Tested

#OpenAI #SamAltman #JonyIve #ChatGPT #AIHardware https://openart.ai/home?utm_source=youtube&utm_medium=influencer&utm_campaign=infl-youtube--na-acq-web&ref=BitBiasedAI-sd25

OpenAI is reportedly building a mysterious $200–$400 AI device with no screen, a voice-first interface, and potentially a camera, environmental sensors, and human-like memory. Sam Altman and legendary Apple designer Jony Ive are behind the project. But there's a major problem: almost everything you've seen about this device could be a rumor, an unverified leak, or an outright fake.

After OpenAI's roughly $6.5 billion acquisition of Jony Ive's AI hardware startup io in May 2025, speculation exploded about what could become OpenAI's first major consumer hardware product. Some reports describe a small, doughnut-shaped or hockey-puck-like AI companion. Others suggest a device that understands its surroundings, remembers conversations, and proactively helps you throughout the day.

But how much of that is actually real?

We break down the credible reporting from Bloomberg, The Verge, MacRumors, and other outlets to separate confirmed developments from anonymous leaks and viral misinformation.

According to reports, OpenAI's mysterious device could feature microphones, speakers, indicator lights, mechanical movement, and possibly a camera. It would likely rely heavily on cloud-based AI rather than running a powerful model entirely on the device. Reported pricing ranges from approximately $200 to $400, with the latest timeline pointing toward early 2027.

And that's where things get complicated.

A screenless ChatGPT device sounds compelling until you consider the limitations. How do you navigate maps, read documents, or review charts without a display? Can an always-listening assistant protect your privacy? What happens when cloud latency interrupts conversations? And can a small battery realistically support continuous AI-powered vision?

Then there's the biggest promise: proactive AI memory.

Reports suggest OpenAI wants an assistant that remembers important details, understands context, and offers help before you even ask. But delivering that experience requires reliable long-term memory, environmental awareness, accurate reasoning, and the ability to take actions without becoming intrusive.

Today's consumer AI devices haven't demonstrated that complete experience reliably.

We also examine Sam Altman's history of ambitious technology investments, from OpenAI and custom AI chips to Helion, Worldcoin, and brain-computer interfaces. His willingness to make enormous bets helps explain why OpenAI is entering the notoriously difficult hardware market.

Jony Ive brings another dimension. After helping shape Apple's iMac, iPod, iPhone, iPad, and Apple Watch, he's now involved in designing a new kind of AI product through LoveFrom. But can world-class industrial design overcome the technical and economic challenges that defeated earlier AI gadgets?

The Humane AI Pin launched at $699 plus a subscription. The Rabbit R1 promised an alternative to smartphone interactions. Both faced criticism over limited functionality and questionable everyday usefulness.

OpenAI will need to prove its device offers something meaningfully better.

We also investigate the viral fake OpenAI Super Bowl advertisement, the mysterious "Dime" puck renders, and the difference between official announcements and convincing fan-made concepts.

Beyond the hardware, there's a much bigger strategic question.

Apple and Google currently control the dominant mobile platforms through which millions of people access AI. An OpenAI-owned device could establish a direct relationship with consumers, potentially connect to ChatGPT subscriptions, and reduce dependence on those platforms.

But hardware manufacturing, cloud inference costs, battery limitations, and privacy concerns could make that strategy extremely expensive.

So is OpenAI preparing the next major shift in personal computing, or another ambitious AI gadget that struggles to justify its existence?

And would you actually pay $300 for a screenless AI companion when ChatGPT already works on your smartphone?

Share your thoughts in the comments, and subscribe to BitBiased for evidence-based coverage of OpenAI, artificial intelligence, emerging technology, and the biggest developments shaping the future of AI.

videos.title: Därför är nya BMW i3 BMW:s viktigaste! Podd: Varför? Därför!
videos.summary_source_text:
Därför är nya BMW i3 BMW:s viktigaste! Podd: Varför? Därför! Nya BMW i3 går 90 mil på en laddning och laddar 40 mil på tio minuter. Men är den verkligen BMW:s viktigaste bil?

I det här avsnittet av Bilpodden Varför? Därför! sitter Felix och jag i nya i3 på slingriga vägar utanför Marseille. Vi pratar om varför 3-serien är så central för BMW och om gamla lilla i3:an, citybilen i kolfiber som fortfarande ser modern ut. Och om hur BMW kan bygga en elbil och en bensinbil som ser likadana ut men inte delar en enda karosspanel.

Vi går igenom 40:an mot 50:an, cylindriska battericeller, 400 kW laddning och Heart of Joy, datorn som ska stå för körglädjen. Sen kör vi. Hur känns styrningen? Bromsarna? Och körassistenten, som tar oss ut på motorvägen utan händer på ratten. Vi tittar också på Panoramic iDrive, baksätet (aj) och hur i3 står sig mot Mercedes CLA, Zeekr 7GT och Tesla Model 3.

Svaret på frågan i rubriken? Kanske inte det du tror. Men den bästa 3-serien någonsin? Där är vi rätt överens.

videos.title: Gemini 4 vs GPT-6 vs Claude 5.5: The $20 AI Subscription WAR
videos.summary_source_text:
Gemini 4 vs GPT-6 vs Claude 5.5: The $20 AI Subscription WAR Google says Gemini 4 Argon beats GPT-6 Astra and Claude Opus 5.5 on 12 out of 18 benchmarks. But independent testing tells a different story. And the AI model with the strongest measured performance at $20 comes with a catch that could make it the wrong subscription for you.

ChatGPT Plus vs Claude Pro vs Google AI Pro vs Grok: which AI subscription actually gives you the most for your money in November 2026?

OpenAI, Google, Anthropic, and xAI have released at least eight new AI models since September 21. GPT-6, GPT-6.1 Sol, Gemini 4 Argon, Claude Opus 5.5, Claude Fable 5.2, and Grok 4.7 are competing for attention. But the best model on a benchmark isn't necessarily the best AI subscription to buy.

Here's where things get interesting.

Google AI Pro costs $19.99 per month and includes Gemini 4 Argon, Google's newest flagship model. You also get a reported 1-million-token context window, 5TB of Google storage, 1,000 monthly Flow credits, and additional Google services. Google's own benchmarks look impressive, but Artificial Analysis scored Argon at 52.6, virtually tied with GPT-6 Astra at 52.7 and behind Claude Opus 5.5 at 57.6.

There's another twist: independent hallucination testing reportedly puts Gemini 4 Argon at 15%, compared with 51% for GPT-6 Astra at maximum reasoning. That could matter enormously for research and fact-heavy work.

Claude Pro costs $20 per month and includes Opus 5.5, the strongest independently measured model in this price comparison. It also includes Claude Code, Research, Projects, and up to 1 million tokens of context depending on the model. videos.title: Round 1 Highlights | 2026 DP World Tour Championship
videos.summary_source_text:
Round 1 Highlights | 2026 DP World Tour Championship Highlights from the opening round at Jumeirah Golf Estates in Dubai as the final event of the DP World Tour season begins at the DP World Tour Championship featuring Rory McIlroy, Jon Rahm, Tyrrell Hatton, Eugenio Chacarra, Ryan Fox and more!

After visiting 25 countries across five continents, the DP World Tour’s schedule reaches a climax this week in Dubai, for the DP World Tour Championship, marking the final event of the 2026 Race to Dubai season. Since 2009, the DP World Tour Championship has annually played host to the season-ending event. Contested over 72 holes, with no cut, the final Rolex Series event features a $10 million prize fund, the biggest of the 2026 Race to Dubai season. 50 players have made their way to the second of back-to-back Rolex Series events, which form the DP World Tour Play-offs. There are two key pieces of silverware on offer this week, The DP World Tour Championship and the Harry Vardon Trophy. The battle for the Race to Dubai title comes to an end this week at Jumeirah Golf Club as players vie to end the year as DP World Tour Number One. There are still nine players in the running to end the year at the top of the Ranking. Eugenio Chacarra, the only three time winner this season, tops the standings heading in with a 533.93 point lead over nearest challenger Rory McIlroy, who is seeking to match Colin Montgomerie’s long-standing record of eight Order of Merit titles this week. With Patrick Reed, Casey Jarvis, US PGA Championship winner Aaron Rai, Jon Rahm, Ryan Fox, Jayden Schaper and Daniel Hillier all are still in with a chance of ending the year as the winner of the season-long race.

videos.title: Flytta vikten med klubban…
videos.channel: Bättre & Enklare golf med Marcus Edblad PGA
videos.summary_source_text:
Flytta vikten med klubban… Forcera inte fram viktförflyttningen utan lita på och låt kroppen naturligt fltta vikten i samspel med hur vi rör klubban.

#golf #golftips #golfswing 

0:00 Intro - Flytta vikten naturligt. 
1:00 Regelbundenhet är nyckeln till framgång. 

Nu finns det möjlighet att genom appen Skillest göra mig till din personliga tränare. Du hittar mig på denna länk: https://skillest.com/app/profile/marcus-edblad

Låt mig hjälpa dig finna bättre slag, bollträff, riktning och svinghastighet. Oavsett om du slår en wedge, järnklubba eller driver kan du med dina händer lära dig golfslag som du inte trodde var möjliga. Längre och rakare slag kräver alltid träning men något alla kan lära sig.  

Vare sig du kämpar med en slice eller en hook så har jag videos som kan guida till bättre golf. Är du nybörjare så kan du börja med min grönt kort eller nybörjarkurs.

Försök ersätta dåliga vanor med nya bättre vanor. Oavsett vilket loft eller skaft din klubba har så är det du som bestämmer vad som ska hända. Oavsett om det står callaway, ping, titleist eller taylor made på klubban så kan du slå bra slag.

Var noga med vad du tittar på. Det finns många duktiga instruktörer på nätet, några av mina favoriter är Mike Malaska, Mike Dunaway, Mike Austin.

Försök fokusera på grunderna i slaget bollträff, bladkontroll och svingspår. Träna med fördel på en sak i taget. Tränar du din svinghastighet måste du tillåta att det går snett och tränar du raka slag kan du inte samtidigt svinga i max fart.

Ha tålamod och låt det ta sin tid, luras inte av genvägar som bara gör att du tappar fokus från det viktiga. Golf kommer alltid vara svårt men vi kan med träning se till att vi blir bättre för varje dag som går.

Titta mycket på golf på TV. Bryson Dechambeu, Dustin Johnson, Rory Mcilroy kan inspirera till längre slag och andra som Tiger Woods, Viktor Hovland, Ludvig Åberg och Phil Mickelson kan ge dig fantasi att skapa nya slag.

Träna styrketräning för hela kroppen för att må bra genom livet och skapa en effektiv maskin. Träna händer, handleder och armar för att skapa en effektiv release och mer svinghastighet.

Du kan finna inspiration i filmer som Happy Gilmore, Tin Cup eller Bagger Vance. Filmer som Rocky kan ge dig motivation att ta dig till gymet. Legender som Arnold Schwarzenegger, Sylvester Stallone eller Hulk Hogan kan få dig att vilja bli starkare och Moe Norman, Arnold Palmer, Ben Hogan, Sam Snead eller Jack Nicklaus kan inspirera dig att bli en bättre golfare. 

Ge aldrig upp i sökandet och träningen för att få bästa bollträff, bladkontroll och svingspår.

Filmat med iPhone 18 och redigerat i iMovie på en Macbook Neo. Forcera inte fram viktförflyttningen utan lita på och låt kroppen naturligt fltta vikten i samspel med hur vi rör klubban.

1:00 Regelbundenhet är nyckeln till framgång. 

Nu finns det möjlighet att genom appen Skillest göra mig till din personliga tränare. Du hittar mig på denna länk: https://skillest.com/app/profile/marcus-edblad

Låt mig hjälpa dig finna bättre slag, bollträff, riktning och svinghastighet. Oavsett om du slår en wedge, järnklubba eller driver kan du med dina händer lära dig golfslag som du inte trodde var möjliga. Längre och rakare slag kräver alltid träning men något alla kan lära sig.  

Vare sig du kämpar med en slice eller en hook så har jag videos som kan guida till bättre golf. Är du nybörjare så kan du börja med min grönt kort eller nybörjarkurs.

Försök ersätta dåliga vanor med nya bättre vanor. Oavsett vilket loft eller skaft din klubba har så är det du som bestämmer vad som ska hända. Oavsett om det står callaway, ping, titleist eller taylor made på klubban så kan du slå bra slag.

Var noga med vad du tittar på. Det finns många duktiga instruktörer på nätet, några av mina favoriter är Mike Malaska, Mike Dunaway, Mike Austin.

Försök fokusera på grunderna i slaget bollträff, bladkontroll och svingspår. Träna med fördel på en sak i taget. Tränar du din svinghastighet måste du tillåta att det går snett och tränar du raka slag kan du inte samtidigt svinga i max fart.

Ha tålamod och låt det ta sin tid, luras inte av genvägar som bara gör att du tappar fokus från det viktiga. Golf kommer alltid vara svårt men vi kan med träning se till att vi blir bättre för varje dag som går.

Titta mycket på golf på TV. Bryson Dechambeu, Dustin Johnson, Rory Mcilroy kan inspirera till längre slag och andra som Tiger Woods, Viktor Hovland, Ludvig Åberg och Phil Mickelson kan ge dig fantasi att skapa nya slag.

Träna styrketräning för hela kroppen för att må bra genom livet och skapa en effektiv maskin. Träna händer, handleder och armar för att skapa en effektiv release och mer svinghastighet.

Du kan finna inspiration i filmer som Happy Gilmore, Tin Cup eller Bagger Vance. Filmer som Rocky kan ge dig motivation att ta dig till gymet. Legender som Arnold Schwarzenegger, Sylvester Stallone eller Hulk Hogan kan få dig att vilja bli starkare och Moe Norman, Arnold Palmer, Ben Hogan, Sam Snead eller Jack Nicklaus kan inspirera dig att bli en bättre golfare. 

Ge aldrig upp i sökandet och träningen för att få bästa bollträff, bladkontroll och svingspår.

Filmat med iPhone 18 och redigerat i iMovie på en Macbook Neo.

videos.title: 11.11.26 - RIFT Training Day
videos.summary_source_text:
11.11.26 - RIFT Training Day RIFT is a modern, non-custodial trading and financial technology ecosystem designed to bring together market access, education, intelligent execution, portfolio participation and professional trading infrastructure in one connected environment.

Built for both newcomers and experienced market participants, RIFT provides a structured journey from learning and practice through to increasingly sophisticated forms of market participation.

ONE ECOSYSTEM. MULTIPLE WAYS TO PARTICIPATE.

RIFT gives users access to a range of trading and financial tools, including:

• Demo Trading — Practice market participation using virtual capital while learning how markets, execution and platform functionality work.

• Spot Trading — Participate directly in spot markets while developing an understanding of market behaviour, patience and risk management.

• Futures Trading — Access leveraged markets with tools and functionality designed for more advanced trading strategies and risk management.

• Smart Money — Explore structured portfolio participation through features including mirror wallets and trading books, allowing users to move beyond focusing only on individual trades.

• Auto Trading Engine — Access structured automated execution through different environments designed to support systematic and repeatable participation.

• Prediction Markets — Participate in an emerging category of market infrastructure where users can trade contracts based on the probability of future events and outcomes.

• Prop Trading Infrastructure — Learn about and participate in the evolving world of proprietary trading, funded accounts, capital allocation, performance evaluation and professional risk management.

INTELLIGENT FINANCIAL INFRASTRUCTURE

RIFT is designed around the idea that the future of finance will combine human decision-making with intelligent technology.

Modern financial markets generate enormous amounts of information. Algorithms and AI systems can process data, identify patterns, monitor markets and support execution at a speed that is impossible for an individual human to replicate.

RIFT explores how these technologies can work alongside human judgement to create more structured and intelligent financial participation.

The objective is not simply to automate everything.

It is to combine people, data, technology, risk management and intelligent execution within a connected financial ecosystem.

EDUCATION AT THE CORE

RIFT places strong emphasis on education and developing a deeper understanding of financial markets.

Through the RIFT Before You Quit educational series, training sessions and community learning, participants explore subjects including:

• Trading psychology
• Risk management
• Capital preservation
• Portfolio construction
• Capital allocation
• Market structure
• Smart money concepts
• Futures and leverage
• Prediction markets
• Proprietary trading
• Behavioural finance
• Artificial intelligence
• Algorithmic execution
• Financial infrastructure

Post-NFL Trade Deadline Reactions + Broncos Bye Week Reflections | MoodSwings Welcome to 'The Morning Liv(e)' show with Liv Moods!

Whether it's on your way to work, while sipping a coffee in your living room, or however else you're spending your morning, if you're looking for a place to get all the latest NFL and NBA news, you're in the right place!

Liv breaks down and discusses the biggest takeaways from the NFL trade deadline, which came and went yesterday, November 10th. The Broncos shocked most fans and made a move right before the deadline, bringing in Chargers LB Daiyan Henley in exchange for a handful of future draft picks. Was this a solid move by Denver? Or did we want to see a bigger move from the front office?

Moving the conversation away from the Broncos, Liv also discusses some other important moves around the league that are worth keeping an eye on. Kirk Cousins LEAVES the AFC West and is heading back to the Minnesota Vikings, his former team, where he hopes to lead the current 6-2 Vikings through the remainder of the season in a gauntlet of an NFC North division, and maybe even make a deep playoff run.

Once the trade deadline officially concluded, a report surfaced that the New York Giants had called the Atlanta Falcons in an attempt to acquire Bijan Robinson before the deadline. Even though the trade didn't go through, you have to give the Giants a TON of credit for how aggressive they've been in making moves over the last year. When your QB goes down, most teams just accept their fate and ride with the backup. But the Giants went out and got JJ McCarthy, who has had a pretty solid campaign in New York so far, minus some injury complications. What would this move have looked like if Bijan DID go to the Giants?

Hosts Chris Micieli and Zach Pearson break down the Avalanche’s winning culture, player treatment, and stable coaching under Joe Sakic’s leadership. The conversation spotlights why Colorado remains a Stanley Cup contender, examines recent underperformers like Scott Wedgewood and Brent Burns, and previews the Avalanche’s challenging matchup against the Ottawa Senators. videos.summary_source_text:
Hindi - 11.11.26 - RIFT Presentation RIFT is a modern, non-custodial trading and financial technology ecosystem designed to bring together market access, education, intelligent execution, portfolio participation and professional trading infrastructure in one connected environment.

Built for both newcomers and experienced market participants, RIFT provides a structured journey from learning and practice through to increasingly sophisticated forms of market participation.

ONE ECOSYSTEM. MULTIPLE WAYS TO PARTICIPATE.

RIFT gives users access to a range of trading and financial tools, including:

• Demo Trading — Practice market participation using virtual capital while learning how markets, execution and platform functionality work.

• Spot Trading — Participate directly in spot markets while developing an understanding of market behaviour, patience and risk management.

• Futures Trading — Access leveraged markets with tools and functionality designed for more advanced trading strategies and risk management.

• Smart Money — Explore structured portfolio participation through features including mirror wallets and trading books, allowing users to move beyond focusing only on individual trades.

• Auto Trading Engine — Access structured automated execution through different environments designed to support systematic and repeatable participation.

• Prediction Markets — Participate in an emerging category of market infrastructure where users can trade contracts based on the probability of future events and outcomes.

• Prop Trading Infrastructure — Learn about and participate in the evolving world of proprietary trading, funded accounts, capital allocation, performance evaluation and professional risk management.

INTELLIGENT FINANCIAL INFRASTRUCTURE

RIFT is designed around the idea that the future of finance will combine human decision-making with intelligent technology.

Modern financial markets generate enormous amounts of information. Algorithms and AI systems can process data, identify patterns, monitor markets and support execution at a speed that is impossible for an individual human to replicate.

RIFT explores how these technologies can work alongside human judgement to create more structured and intelligent financial participation.

The objective is not simply to automate everything.

It is to combine people, data, technology, risk management and intelligent execution within a connected financial ecosystem.

EDUCATION AT THE CORE

RIFT places strong emphasis on education and developing a deeper understanding of financial markets.

Through the RIFT Before You Quit educational series, training sessions and community learning, participants explore subjects including:

• Trading psychology
• Risk management
• Capital preservation
• Portfolio construction
• Capital allocation
• Market structure
• Smart money concepts
• Futures and leverage
• Prediction markets
• Proprietary trading
• Behavioural finance
• Artificial intelligence
• Algorithmic execution
• Financial infrastructure
• Professional trading principles

The objective is to help participants understand not only how to participate in markets, but also why disciplined decision-making matters.

A STRUCTURED LEARNING JOURNEY

RIFT is designed to provide a progression from education and practice toward more advanced market participation:

Learn → Demo → Spot → Futures → Smart Money → Automated Execution → Professional Trading

Each stage introduces different concepts, technologies and levels of responsibility.

Rather than focusing solely on individual trades or short-term results, RIFT encourages participants to develop a broader understanding of risk, process, discipline and capital management.

NON-CUSTODIAL INFRASTRUCTURE

RIFT follows a non-custodial approach designed to give users greater control over their own funds and reduce the need to place assets into a centralized company-controlled account.

This reflects a broader movement within digital finance toward greater transparency, user control and blockchain-based infrastructure.

ACCESS FROM ANY DEVICE

RIFT is available through the web as well as its broader platform environment, making it accessible across modern computers, smartphones and other devices.

Its lightweight infrastructure is designed to make participation practical even for users with older devices, helping remove unnecessary technology barriers to accessing modern financial tools.

THE FUTURE OF FINANCIAL PARTICIPATION

Financial markets are changing rapidly.

Trading is becoming increasingly automated. Artificial intelligence is transforming data analysis. Prediction markets are creating new forms of information-based participation. Proprietary trading is expanding access to structured capital allocation models. Blockchain infrastructure is changing how digital assets can be held and transferred.

RIFT brings these developments together within one evolving ecosystem.

videos.title: Bump, Turn, Bump, Turn” Move (Like Tiger 2000)
videos.summary_source_text:
Bump, Turn, Bump, Turn” Move (Like Tiger 2000) Does your downswing feel like it’s all arms? Your weight shift might be a beat late.
Bump, turn. Bump, turn. That’s the rhythm to watch for in Tiger Woods’ 2000 swing. Here’s how I practice it with the Ball First Board.

Which BTW we have the loweeeest price on the Ball First Board right here!

https://improve.shotcraftgolf.com/products/bfb/lp2?utm_source=youtube&utm_medium=social&utm_content=youtube-short-BumpTurnTiger

1️⃣ Before the backswing, press into your trail foot, then turn. Keep the bump small enough that you don’t sway into the alignment stick.

2️⃣ Before your arms start down, feel a slight squat as you shift pressure into your lead foot. Then turn through and let your arms follow.

🔖 Save this golf swing drill for your next range session. Before you hit your first ball, make three slow practice swings and say “bump, turn, bump, turn” as you go.

• Parsley: Supports fluid balance and has anti-inflammatory properties

Topped shots and inconsistent contact from one day to the next usually come from standing up or lifting during the golf swing, and it's what Eric Cogorno sees every day in golf lessons with regular golfers. When your shoulders turn too level, your body moves farther from the ground, and constantly getting farther from and closer to the ground is the least consistent way to play. The fix is shoulder tilt: your left shoulder goes down and in and under your chin in the backswing, about 40°, and your right shoulder goes down with even more tilt, about 55°, in the golf downswing, the same pattern you see in Tommy Fleetwood's golf swing. These golf swing tips and a simple golf drill with a second ball about one yard outside the first show you how much tilt to feel, so you can build a consistent golf swing and learn how to hit irons solid. If you leave this video without trying this golf drill, you're leaving solid, consistent contact on the table.

• Why standing up in your golf swing leads to topped shots

• What the Tommy Fleetwood swing shows about left shoulder tilt

• Why you need more tilt in the golf downswing than the backswing
• Golf tips to keep your height going back and get lower coming down
• Why you have to exaggerate a feel to make a real change

Topped shots and inconsistent contact from one day to the next usually come from standing up or lifting during the golf swing, and it's what Eric Cogorno sees every day in golf lessons with regular golfers. When your shoulders turn too level, your body moves farther from the ground, and constantly getting farther from and closer to the ground is the least consistent way to play. The fix is shoulder tilt: your left shoulder goes down and in and under your chin in the backswing, about 40°, and your right shoulder goes down with even more tilt, about 55°, in the golf downswing, the same pattern you see in Tommy Fleetwood's golf swing. These golf swing tips and a simple golf drill with a second ball about one yard outside the first show you how much tilt to feel, so you can build a consistent golf swing and learn how to hit irons solid. If you leave this video without trying this golf drill, you're leaving solid, consistent contact on the table.

Even after menopause, your ovaries continue to produce important hormones, including estrogen, progesterone, testosterone, and DHEA. A hysterectomy can affect blood flow to the ovaries and potentially disrupt hormone production even when the ovaries aren’t removed.

Unlike natural menopause, which happens gradually, hormonal changes after a hysterectomy can occur suddenly, giving the body less time to adapt.

Hysterectomy side effects may include:
• Hot flashes, night sweats, and poor sleep
• Mood changes and cognitive problems
• Bladder and bowel problems
• Increased cardiovascular risk
• Bone loss and osteoporosis
• Insulin resistance and visceral fat
• Muscle loss and joint pain

Hormonal changes after a hysterectomy may also affect nitric oxide production, inflammation, and long-term health.

To support your health and hormones after a hysterectomy, focus on intermittent fasting and a low-carb diet with high-quality animal protein.

videos.summary_source_text:
I Tried to Vibe Code Zapier (Claude Code) Try my exact Zap in Zapier (one click and Copilot builds it): https://mrc.fm/vibecode
The clone prompt from Can I Vibecode It: https://mrc.fm/vibecodeprompt

I gave Claude Code one prompt from Can I Vibecode It and it built me my own Zapier clone in about four and a half minutes, on a five dollar server. Webhooks, schedules, retries, a run log, alerts. Then I sent the same leads to my clone and to Zapier, and fast forwarded through six months of real life: logins that expire, a teammate renaming a tab, a server going down, a Node.js update, a full disk, and a month of security patches.

My clone failed again and again. Zapier kept every single lead.

Claude Code didn't write bad code. The problem is everything around the code. That's not building, that's maintaining, and maintaining never ends.

This video is sponsored by Zapier.

What would you vibe code, and what would you never trust to a weekend project? Tell me in the comments.

videos.title: Bruno Senna: How Ayrton Inspires A New Generation | F1 Beyond The Grid Podcast
videos.summary_source_text:
Bruno Senna: How Ayrton Inspires A New Generation | F1 Beyond The Grid Podcast An icon of Formula 1, a three-time World Champion, and a hero even to those who never saw him race. More than three decades after his death, Ayrton Senna remains an inspiration for F1 drivers and fans all over the world.

Bruno Senna, Ayrton’s nephew and former F1 driver, tells Tom Clarkson about Kimi Antonelli’s recent trip to the Senna family farm, when the 2026 World Champion sat in one of Ayrton’s cars and drove on a go-kart track he designed.

Bruno tells the story of Ayrton’s famous victory at home in 1991, when he screamed in exhausted celebration after winning the Brazilian Grand Prix in a car stuck in sixth gear. He remembers how Ayrton taught him to fight on track – preparation for Bruno’s own F1 career with Hispania, Lotus and Williams in the early 2010s.

Bruno also explains the work of the Senna Foundation, which has helped to educate 30 million children in Brazil since it was founded, and hails today’s Brazilian F1 stars – Gabriel Bortoleto and Rafael Camara.

After 40 events, five global swings, the Back 9 and four Majors, the DP World Tour Play-Offs are upon us. The top 70 available players from the Race to Dubai Rankings Delivered by DP World tee it up this week at Yas Links before the top 50 then move on to the season-finale at the DP World Tour Championship. Both those events form part of the Rolex Series, with Patrick Reed, Tom Kim and JJ Spaun having already been crowned Rolex Series champions in 2026. With full playing privileges on the DP World Tour now secured the focus turns to the quest to be Europe’s Number One and claim the Harry Vardon Trophy. Rory McIlroy is looking to equal Colin Montgomerie's record of eight season-long wins with his fifth in a row but the Northern Irishman is in the unusual position of being the hunter rather than the hunted. Last year, Aaron Rai beat fellow Englishman Tommy Fleetwood in a play-off to win his second Rolex Series title at Yas Links, five years on from his first at the Scottish Open. videos.title: 10.11.26 - RIFT Presentation
videos.summary_source_text:
10.11.26 - RIFT Presentation RIFT is a modern, non-custodial trading and financial technology ecosystem designed to bring together market access, education, intelligent execution, portfolio participation and professional trading infrastructure in one connected environment.

Built for both newcomers and experienced market participants, RIFT provides a structured journey from learning and practice through to increasingly sophisticated forms of market participation.

ONE ECOSYSTEM. MULTIPLE WAYS TO PARTICIPATE.

RIFT gives users access to a range of trading and financial tools, including:

• Demo Trading — Practice market participation using virtual capital while learning how markets, execution and platform functionality work.

• Spot Trading — Participate directly in spot markets while developing an understanding of market behaviour, patience and risk management.

• Futures Trading — Access leveraged markets with tools and functionality designed for more advanced trading strategies and risk management.

• Smart Money — Explore structured portfolio participation through features including mirror wallets and trading books, allowing users to move beyond focusing only on individual trades.

• Auto Trading Engine — Access structured automated execution through different environments designed to support systematic and repeatable participation.

• Prediction Markets — Participate in an emerging category of market infrastructure where users can trade contracts based on the probability of future events and outcomes.

• Prop Trading Infrastructure — Learn about and participate in the evolving world of proprietary trading, funded accounts, capital allocation, performance evaluation and professional risk management.

INTELLIGENT FINANCIAL INFRASTRUCTURE

RIFT is designed around the idea that the future of finance will combine human decision-making with intelligent technology.

Modern financial markets generate enormous amounts of information. Algorithms and AI systems can process data, identify patterns, monitor markets and support execution at a speed that is impossible for an individual human to replicate.

RIFT explores how these technologies can work alongside human judgement to create more structured and intelligent financial participation.

The objective is not simply to automate everything.

It is to combine people, data, technology, risk management and intelligent execution within a connected financial ecosystem.

EDUCATION AT THE CORE

RIFT places strong emphasis on education and developing a deeper understanding of financial markets.

Through the RIFT Before You Quit educational series, training sessions and community learning, participants explore subjects including:

• Trading psychology
• Risk management
• Capital preservation
• Portfolio construction
• Capital allocation
• Market structure
• Smart money concepts
• Futures and leverage
• Prediction markets
• Proprietary trading
• Behavioural finance
• Artificial intelligence
• Algorithmic execution
• Financial infrastructure
• Professional trading principles

The objective is to help participants understand not only how to participate in markets, but also why disciplined decision-making matters.

A STRUCTURED LEARNING JOURNEY

RIFT is designed to provide a progression from education and practice toward more advanced market participation:

Learn → Demo → Spot → Futures → Smart Money → Automated Execution → Professional Trading

Each stage introduces different concepts, technologies and levels of responsibility.

Rather than focusing solely on individual trades or short-term results, RIFT encourages participants to develop a broader understanding of risk, process, discipline and capital management.

NON-CUSTODIAL INFRASTRUCTURE

RIFT follows a non-custodial approach designed to give users greater control over their own funds and reduce the need to place assets into a centralized company-controlled account.

This reflects a broader movement within digital finance toward greater transparency, user control and blockchain-based infrastructure.

ACCESS FROM ANY DEVICE

RIFT is available through the web as well as its broader platform environment, making it accessible across modern computers, smartphones and other devices.

Its lightweight infrastructure is designed to make participation practical even for users with older devices, helping remove unnecessary technology barriers to accessing modern financial tools.

THE FUTURE OF FINANCIAL PARTICIPATION

Financial markets are changing rapidly.

Trading is becoming increasingly automated. Artificial intelligence is transforming data analysis. Prediction markets are creating new forms of information-based participation. Proprietary trading is expanding access to structured capital allocation models. Blockchain infrastructure is changing how digital assets can be held and transferred.

RIFT brings these developments together within one evolving ecosystem.

videos.title: Avalanche Avenge 6-3 Loss to Maple Leafs With a 6-3 Win In Toronto
videos.summary_source_text:
Avalanche Avenge 6-3 Loss to Maple Leafs With a 6-3 Win In Toronto Colorado Avalanche overpower the Toronto Maple Leafs with a commanding 6-3 victory, even with Nathan MacKinnon’s name missing from the scoresheet. Is Colorado’s offensive depth the key to another deep postseason run?

The conversation focused on the Avalanche’s balanced attack, standout plays from Devon Toews and Gabe Landeskog, and Nazem Kadri’s pinpoint passing in key moments. Analysis covered Toronto’s struggle to contain Colorado’s third line, detailed player stat breakdowns—including William Nylander’s invisible night—and the impact of Mackenzie Blackwood’s sharp goaltending. A key theme that emerged was how the Avs twice responded to Leafs’ surges, sealing the win with timely goals and relentless forechecking. The discussion explored lineup adjustments, strategic momentum shifts, and the implications of Denver’s growing confidence as playoff season nears.

Can the Maple Leafs bounce back from another home defeat, or is Colorado’s depth too much for contenders to handle?

Nick Turchiaro-Imagn Images

videos.title: Hindi - 10.11.26 - RIFT Presentation
videos.summary_source_text:
Hindi - 10.11.26 - RIFT Presentation RIFT is a modern, non-custodial trading and financial technology ecosystem designed to bring together market access, education, intelligent execution, portfolio participation and professional trading infrastructure in one connected environment.

Built for both newcomers and experienced market participants, RIFT provides a structured journey from learning and practice through to increasingly sophisticated forms of market participation.

ONE ECOSYSTEM. MULTIPLE WAYS TO PARTICIPATE.

RIFT gives users access to a range of trading and financial tools, including:

• Demo Trading — Practice market participation using virtual capital while learning how markets, execution and platform functionality work.

• Spot Trading — Participate directly in spot markets while developing an understanding of market behaviour, patience and risk management.

• Futures Trading — Access leveraged markets with tools and functionality designed for more advanced trading strategies and risk management.

• Smart Money — Explore structured portfolio participation through features including mirror wallets and trading books, allowing users to move beyond focusing only on individual trades.

• Auto Trading Engine — Access structured automated execution through different environments designed to support systematic and repeatable participation.

• Prediction Markets — Participate in an emerging category of market infrastructure where users can trade contracts based on the probability of future events and outcomes.

• Prop Trading Infrastructure — Learn about and participate in the evolving world of proprietary trading, funded accounts, capital allocation, performance evaluation and professional risk management.

INTELLIGENT FINANCIAL INFRASTRUCTURE

RIFT is designed around the idea that the future of finance will combine human decision-making with intelligent technology.

Modern financial markets generate enormous amounts of information. Algorithms and AI systems can process data, identify patterns, monitor markets and support execution at a speed that is impossible for an individual human to replicate.

RIFT explores how these technologies can work alongside human judgement to create more structured and intelligent financial participation.

The objective is not simply to automate everything.

It is to combine people, data, technology, risk management and intelligent execution within a connected financial ecosystem.

EDUCATION AT THE CORE

RIFT places strong emphasis on education and developing a deeper understanding of financial markets.

Through the RIFT Before You Quit educational series, training sessions and community learning, participants explore subjects including:

• Trading psychology
• Risk management
• Capital preservation
• Portfolio construction
• Capital allocation
• Market structure
• Smart money concepts
• Futures and leverage
• Prediction markets
• Proprietary trading
• Behavioural finance
• Artificial intelligence
• Algorithmic execution
• Financial infrastructure
• Professional trading principles

The objective is to help participants understand not only how to participate in markets, but also why disciplined decision-making matters.

A STRUCTURED LEARNING JOURNEY

RIFT is designed to provide a progression from education and practice toward more advanced market participation:

Learn → Demo → Spot → Futures → Smart Money → Automated Execution → Professional Trading

Each stage introduces different concepts, technologies and levels of responsibility.

Rather than focusing solely on individual trades or short-term results, RIFT encourages participants to develop a broader understanding of risk, process, discipline and capital management.

NON-CUSTODIAL INFRASTRUCTURE

RIFT follows a non-custodial approach designed to give users greater control over their own funds and reduce the need to place assets into a centralized company-controlled account.

This reflects a broader movement within digital finance toward greater transparency, user control and blockchain-based infrastructure.

ACCESS FROM ANY DEVICE

RIFT is available through the web as well as its broader platform environment, making it accessible across modern computers, smartphones and other devices.

Its lightweight infrastructure is designed to make participation practical even for users with older devices, helping remove unnecessary technology barriers to accessing modern financial tools.

THE FUTURE OF FINANCIAL PARTICIPATION

Financial markets are changing rapidly.

Trading is becoming increasingly automated. Artificial intelligence is transforming data analysis. Prediction markets are creating new forms of information-based participation. Proprietary trading is expanding access to structured capital allocation models. Blockchain infrastructure is changing how digital assets can be held and transferred.

RIFT brings these developments together within one evolving ecosystem.

Some bacterial strains may never fully recover, affecting the balance of microbes involved in immunity, mood, metabolism, and vitamin production.

🌟 Take the 2-minute Health Lever Quiz: https://drbrg.co/47fqfe1

Disruptions to the gut microbiome after antibiotics can contribute to:
• Gut inflammation
• Brain fog
• Changes in mood
• Digestive problems
• Reduced microbial diversity
• Candida and yeast overgrowth

Antibiotics kill bacteria, but they don’t eliminate yeast or fungi. Taking probiotics and consuming fermented foods during and after antibiotics is vital for restoring beneficial gut bacteria to keep bad bacteria, yeast, and fungi in check.

videos.summary_source_text:
The Amazing Benefits of Iodine Iodine is essential for much more than thyroid health. Every cell in your body needs iodine, with significant amounts concentrated in the breast tissue, ovaries, brain, stomach lining, and eyes.

Watch the FULL video here: https://youtu.be/MhUgmTCJyiE

🌟 Take Dr. Berg’s New Health Quiz—60 seconds is all it takes: https://drbrg.co/4BR1UsO

Iodine plays several important roles in the body, including:
• Supporting thyroid hormone production
• Helping regulate estrogen activity
• Supporting breast and reproductive health
• Strengthening immune function
• Reducing inflammation
• Supporting healthy brain development during pregnancy

Iodine intake has also been studied for its relationship to breast and prostate cancer risk. Getting enough iodine is especially important during pregnancy when deficiency can affect fetal development.

In this video, Dr. Mandell explains how plaque develops inside artery walls and builds a practical heart-supporting meal with leafy greens, tomatoes, beans, salmon, and extra-virgin olive oil. You’ll learn how soluble fiber can help lower LDL cholesterol, why replacing some saturated fat with unsaturated fat matters, and how the Mediterranean-style eating pattern has been studied for cardiovascular health. videos.title: What Dementia Does to Your Brain?
videos.summary_source_text:
What Dementia Does to Your Brain? Walked into a room and forgot why? That on its own isn't dementia. In this calm, evidence-based guide you'll learn the difference between ordinary forgetfulness and the 8 warning signs that are worth a doctor's visit. You'll also learn the treatable "look-alikes": low vitamin B12, a slow thyroid, medicine side effects, delirium and depression. We cover how depression and anxiety show up in later life, clear up three common myths, and finish with six steps the research supports, from protecting your hearing to knowing your blood-pressure numbers.

- 7:48 When to see a doctor
- 8:40 Recap

videos.title: OpenAI's GPT-6.2 Preview Is Insane: It Just Beat Fable 5.2!
videos.summary_source_text:
OpenAI's GPT-6.2 Preview Is Insane: It Just Beat Fable 5.2! https://openart.ai/home?utm_source=youtube&utm_medium=influencer&utm_campaign=infl-youtube--na-acq-web&ref=BitBiasedAI-sd25

GPT-6.2 has reportedly appeared inside OpenAI's own Codex usage dashboard, with one developer seeing the mysterious model name account for 37.7% of a day's usage. But OpenAI hasn't announced GPT-6.2, the model picker hasn't changed, and developers can't access it through the public API.

So what exactly is OpenAI testing? And could GPT-6.2 be the company's answer to Anthropic's newly launched Claude Fable 5.2?

The timing is hard to ignore. GPT-6.2 sightings began around November 1, just eight days before Anthropic launched Fable 5.2 on November 9. According to Anthropic's published benchmarks, Fable 5.2 scored 49.1% on FrontierCode 2.0, compared with 42.8% for OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra. That's a 6.3-point advantage on a major coding evaluation.

The computer-use numbers are even more striking. On OSWorld 2.1, Anthropic reports Fable 5.2 reaching 89.3%, while GPT-6 Astra scores 79.5%.

But those results come from Anthropic's own testing, with important methodological limitations. And there's currently no independently verified GPT-6.2 benchmark to compare against them.

That's where the mystery begins.

Screenshots collected by TestingCatalog show a model labeled "gpt-6.2-astra" appearing in Codex analytics. Different users reportedly saw it accounting for 1.6%, 19.8%, and even 37.7% of their usage. Yet nobody could deliberately select GPT-6.2, and direct API requests reportedly returned model-not-found errors.

Could this be an internal canary deployment, an experimental routing system, or simply a backend label that doesn't represent a new model?

There's also a critical technical distinction most viral posts overlook: a model identifier appearing in a log isn't necessarily proof that a corresponding model actually processed the request. Some interfaces can echo arbitrary model names, making screenshots far less conclusive than they initially appear.

And the rumors don't stop with Astra.

Names including GPT-6.2 Sol, Bel, Beetlejuice, and Betelgeuse have circulated across Reddit, Discord, and social media. One anonymous claim even describes a model exceeding 10 trillion parameters. None of these claims currently has authenticated documentation or independently reproducible evidence.

Then came the viral demonstrations: a 360-degree 3D pelican riding a bicycle, a semi-open-world RPG supposedly generated from one prompt, browser automation experiments, and logic puzzles allegedly showing GPT-6.2 outperforming Claude.

Impressive? Potentially. Verified as GPT-6.2 outputs? Not yet.

We examine why these demonstrations don't establish model identity, why a single spectacular output isn't a meaningful benchmark, and what a legitimate head-to-head comparison would actually require.

Meanwhile, OpenAI's documented releases tell a different story. GPT-6 Astra, GPT-6.1 Sol, Luna, Terra, and GPT-6 Cyber show a strategy focused on faster inference, lower costs, specialized capabilities, and expanded context windows.

GPT-6.1 Terra reportedly delivers performance comparable to Astra at around one-tenth the price per token, while GPT-6 Cyber introduces a 1.05-million-token context window for security customers.

So is GPT-6.2 an imminent breakthrough, a quiet internal experiment, or an ordinary infrastructure label amplified into a major AI launch rumor?

And more importantly, what would OpenAI actually need to achieve to overtake Claude Fable 5.2?

We break down the leaked Codex evidence, Anthropic's benchmark claims, the questionable GPT-6.2 demonstrations, competing model releases, and the crucial difference between a possible test and a verified breakthrough.

Because until an official model card, accessible API, and reproducible benchmarks appear, the biggest GPT-6.2 claims remain exactly that: claims.

Subscribe to BitBiased for evidence-driven coverage of OpenAI, Anthropic, artificial intelligence, emerging technology, and the competition shaping the future of AI.
